synopsis: Caterpillar provides a precedent for restricted-domain release: Cat Detect automatic braking launched on medium wheel loaders in May 2025 with reverse-only operation, although Chapter 2 separately reports that no wheel-loader AEB launch date was found [f1067, f1068, f1632, f73]. The loader system inhibits reverse engagement after at least 15 seconds stationary when an object is in the critical zone, and adjusts warning levels with ground speed to reduce nuisance alarms [f10637, f10636]. Asphalt-compactor collision mitigation extends coverage to forward and reverse; it was shown in March 2026 and reported on 29 May 2026 as slated for launch by midyear, rather than confirmed launched [f1070, f1071]. Caterpillar warns that camera-based detection may miss crouching or lying people and can be impaired by low light, snow, rain or fog [f1638]. Warning-event and GPS logging offers a data path for shadow-mode validation, but no independent performance test was found, published validation methods and timelines remain unavailable, and the case's evidence acceptance was internal [f1603, f1242, f1389, f1867].
